item: Test replacements of os functions are bound to the module under test (scope_os), with a guard; two low notes of the #1596 read closed
summary: R351. About 120 call sites in 47 test files that replaced an os function for the whole process (monkeypatch.setattr(module.os, 'replace', f) patches os itself, the test runner and every thread included; R344/R350) now replace the name the module under test reads through tests/os_scope.py (scope_os, hide_os); tests/test_os_patches_are_scoped.py reads every test file's AST (attribute, string target and patch.object forms) and fails outside a three-entry allowlist of deliberate guards (os.kill x2, the /proc open spy), and on a stale entry; six string-target files the 2026-10-27 grep missed were found by it. Ten tests went red on the first scoping because the code under test writes through src.safety.file_lock (scoped there); the whole set was then run once under a throwaway call-counting plugin: 14 of the replacements are never called, 12 by design, 1 vacuous before this change, 1 never reached (details in the lesson). Also: a test that fails when the ContextVar reset in the briefing rebuild is removed, and the quiesce fixture waits for a briefing thread that has no ident yet instead of skipping it (both red against their mutants). Stated: os.path, os.environ and builtins patches are other shapes and were not swept; the touched files were run, not the whole suite.
